hood_desc: A fashionable historic district of medieval lanes, chic boutiques, art galleries, falafel spots, and a lively LGBTQ+ scene, suiting trendy travelers, shoppers, and foodies.
An elegant Left Bank literary quarter of storied cafes, galleries, and upscale boutiques, ideal for sophisticated travelers seeking classic Parisian charm.
The hilltop artists' village crowned by the Sacré-Coeur basilica, with winding cobbled streets and bohemian cafes, perfect for romantics and sightseers seeking postcard views.
A lively student district around the Sorbonne with bookshops, bistros, and Roman ruins, appealing to budget travelers, intellectuals, and those wanting a youthful buzz.
The grand tree-lined avenue of flagship stores, cinemas, and cafes leading to the Arc de Triomphe, drawing luxury shoppers and first-time sightseers.
lodging: Young & Happy Latin Quarter by Hiphophostels

water.note: Tap water is safe and closely monitored; a Parisian classic is asking for 'une carafe d'eau'.

transit.pay: Paper tickets are gone: buy a reloadable Navigo Easy card (€2, ~US$2.30) at station machines and counters, or buy tickets on your phone via the Île-de-France Mobilités app. Flat fares apply region-wide: €2.50 (~US$2.90) for metro/RER trips, €2 for bus/tram. Contactless bank-card payment works only on some buses so far — not in the metro.
transit.hours: The Métro runs about 5:30am to 1:15am (until ~2:15am Fri–Sat); Noctilien night buses run overnight.

landmarks: Eiffel Tower
The wrought-iron 1889 tower is Paris's defining symbol and offers sweeping city views from its summit, especially striking at sunset or when its lights sparkle after dark.
Louvre Museum
The world's most-visited museum, fronted by I.M. Pei's glass pyramid, houses the Mona Lisa and Venus de Milo and is a favorite photo spot at dawn or dusk.
Notre-Dame Cathedral
This masterpiece of French Gothic architecture on the Île de la Cité, famed for its flying buttresses and rose windows, remains one of the most photographed churches in the world.
Arc de Triomphe
Napoleon's monumental triumphal arch anchors the Champs-Élysées and offers a rooftop panorama down twelve radiating avenues.
Sacré-Cœur Basilica
Perched atop Montmartre with gleaming white travertine domes, this basilica gives one of the best panoramic views over Paris's rooftops.
Champs-Élysées
Dubbed 'the world's most beautiful avenue,' this grand boulevard links the Arc de Triomphe to Place de la Concorde with iconic shops, cafés, and lighting displays.
Musée d'Orsay
Housed in a converted Belle Époque railway station, this museum holds the world's largest collection of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist masterpieces.
Panthéon
This domed neoclassical monument in the Latin Quarter entombs French luminaries like Voltaire, Rousseau, and Marie Curie beneath a soaring interior.
Pont Alexandre III
Widely considered Paris's most ornate bridge, its gilded statues, Art Nouveau lamps, and Seine views make it a favorite for photographers.
Sainte-Chapelle
A Gothic royal chapel on the Île de la Cité famed for its soaring stained-glass windows, built in the 13th century to house relics of the Crown of Thorns.

train.note: Each direction has its own terminus: Gare du Nord for Eurostar and European Sleeper, Gare de Lyon for Switzerland and Italy, Gare de l'Est for Germany, and Gare de Lyon or Montparnasse for Spain depending on the service. OBB's Nightjet sleepers to Vienna and Berlin were withdrawn in late 2025, but European Sleeper's Paris-Brussels-Berlin night train took over in March 2026; domestic Intercites de Nuit sleepers leave from Gare d'Austerlitz. Eurostar passengers clear UK passport control and security before boarding, so arrive at least 60-90 minutes early. Booking windows open around four to six months ahead and the cheapest fares go quickly on Eurostar, Lyria and the Barcelona trains.

intl.to: London, Brussels, Amsterdam & other European cities

bus.note: Most international coaches use the Paris-Bercy Seine coach station on metro line 14 and line 6 at Bercy; some also call at Paris-La Defense or Porte Maillot. Tickets are bought online or through the operators' apps rather than at a counter. Bring your passport for UK-bound buses - border checks are made before the Channel crossing and a UK ETA is now needed for most nationalities. London is about 8-9 hours by coach, Brussels 4 and Amsterdam 7.

ferry.note: Paris is inland on the Seine, so there are no international ferries - only Batobus river shuttles, sightseeing bateaux-mouches and long-distance river cruises. The nearest Channel ferry ports are Calais, Dieppe and Le Havre, all reachable by direct train in two to three hours, with onward sailings to Dover, Newhaven and Portsmouth.
